title: Pair-duplication machine
statement: There is a deterministic Boolean Turing machine with no work tapes and five states, numbered $0$ through $4$, whose initial state is $0$. Its transition rules are as follows: in state $0$, on a Boolean input symbol $b$, it emits $b$ and enters state $1$ without moving the input head; on blank it moves left, emits false, and enters state $2$. In state $1$ it moves right, emits the scanned symbol if present, and returns to state $0$. In state $2$, it moves left while reading symbols, and on blank moves right into state $3$. In state $3$ it emits true and enters state $4$ without moving; in state $4$ it moves right and emits each scanned symbol, halting on blank.
hypotheses_covered: Transition behavior on each state and scanned-symbol case
